title: Repeated health-check polling output buries a real incident finding
notes: Long runs of near-identical health-check polling output bury a real incident finding (a downstream dependency intermittently failing health checks). Tests junk resistance.

turns.text: Can you poll the health endpoint for the notifications-service every few seconds for a bit and see if it's stable? Support says users are seeing intermittent notification delays.

Interesting — the service reports 'ok' most of the time, but flips to 'degraded' with reason 'queue-consumer-lag' roughly every 15 polls, i.e. roughly every 45 seconds, for a single poll cycle each time. That intermittent pattern matches the delay complaints — it's not down, it's periodically backing up.

I'd need to check the consumer's own metrics next, but the periodic ~45-second cadence suggests something batch-like is running on that interval and briefly starving the notification consumer of CPU or DB connections — worth checking for a scheduled job on roughly that period.
OK, log that finding and I'll have the notifications team dig into what's running every 45 seconds.
Logged. Recommending the notifications team check for a scheduled job with a roughly 45-second period that could be starving the queue consumer of CPU or DB connections during those windows.

gold_atoms.text: notifications-service health checks reported 'degraded' with reason 'queue-consumer-lag' roughly every 45 seconds (about every 15 polls at a 3-second poll interval), otherwise reporting 'ok' — matching the intermittent notification-delay complaints from support.
The periodic ~45-second degraded cadence suggests a batch-like scheduled job running on that interval is briefly starving the notifications queue consumer of CPU or DB connections.
Have the notifications team investigate whether a scheduled job runs on a roughly 45-second period and could be starving the queue consumer during degraded windows.
